title: Results hand off as F13LD.tpms recipes in the URL, with normalization flags always written
context: 43-handoff.js opens F13LD.mesh with ?r=<recipe JSON> and F13LD.lab with #r=, or copies the JSON. Recipes follow F13LD.tpms v1.1.0 and always write shell_normalize / pi_normalize, because Mesh and Sweep default a missing flag to on and Lab to off.

options.name: Recipe JSON in the URL, flags explicit (current)
options.summary: No server; the recipe is the whole contract.
pros: Explicit flags fixed PI-TPMS building at 3 to 4× predicted density in Lab
cons: Long URLs; tools disagree on defaults, so every writer must remember the flags

options.name: Recipe schema with a version and required flags
options.summary: Make the flags mandatory in the recipe spec and have readers reject or warn on missing ones.
pros: Fixes the default mismatch at the source
cons: Needs changes in Mesh, Lab and Sweep

recommendation: README "Recipes say how they are normalized" and the v0.3.0 recap; implemented in 10-encoding.js (recipe writer) and 43-handoff.js.

log_refs.entry: Architecture notes: Recipes say how they are normalized
